rubric.0: unusable -- wrong task, structurally nonsensical, or dangerous
rubric.1: major repair required -- core idea recognizable but significant graph repair needed
rubric.2: useful with minor modification -- mostly correct but an operator would realistically edit it
rubric.3: accept-ready -- good enough to Accept directly

cases.notes: Detached E_N01_CONTINUE, inserted one research/synthesis node, re-routed into the existing review. Minimal, exactly matched the ask. Real Accept+Save+Run verified (see planner_accept_run_v0_2.json, label simple_A): executed N01->N03->N02->N09, settled WAITING_FOR_HUMAN.

Fan-out into two branches converging on a MERGE was structurally correct (ALL_MATCHES, closed incoming set), but the MERGE node was given role=RESEARCH_SYNTHESIZER, which only IMPLEMENT/REVIEW/REPAIR nodes may carry. A single-field deletion would make this Accept-ready -- the clearest Modify-candidate in the corpus.
cases.before_after: BEFORE the role/capability/effort clarification rule (see repair #2 below).

cases.notes: AFTER adding the role/capability/effort-is-conditional-on-type rule to the planning package: same case, same profile, now PROPOSAL_READY (4 nodes, legal MERGE). Real Accept+Save+Run verified (planner_accept_run_v0_2.json, label branch_merge_B): executed N01->{N03,N04}->N05(MERGE)->N06->N02->N09, settled WAITING_FOR_HUMAN. This is the required branch+MERGE real-run evidence.

Same mistake as SOL_HIGH (role on the MERGE node), same case -- cross-model evidence this failure mode is not one provider's quirk. Run before the repair rule existed; not re-tested under OPUS_HIGH after the fix (budget).

Asked for one implementation step + a review that can route into repair; the model built a 6-node IMPLEMENT/REVIEW/REPAIR/REVIEW/MERGE/FINAL_GATE structure and gave the MERGE a role (second, unreported instance of the same defect class -- validation stops at first failure so a FINAL_GATE with the same mistake was never even reached). Over-scoped relative to the ask as well as invalid; not a clean Modify case.
Detached the conditional E_N02_PASS edge (not an unconditional one -- a different splice shape than A/B/E), inserted one documentation node, preserved the PASS condition into it and on to N09. Clean.

Detached the anchor's sole unconditional edge and re-routed through a new node whose two outgoing edges use mutually-exclusive has_findings True/False predicates -- avoids the FIRST_MATCH unconditional-shadows-conditional hazard entirely rather than triggering it. No unrequested REPAIR/BLOCKED wiring was invented beyond what was asked.

Also correct and legal, with a bounded REPAIR loop added for the compliance check (not strictly requested) and exceptionally thorough self-flagged warnings (fan-in reachability under FIRST_MATCH, cycle avoidance, whether the runtime lets a REVIEW report has_findings independently of verdict). Higher reasoning depth, more elaborate than the minimum, ~3x SOL_HIGH's wall time.

Expected a refusal (splicing before an existing MERGE); instead the model detached E_N05_CONTINUE and re-declared an edge with the SAME edge_id from the new review node to M08 -- M08's expected_incoming stays byte-identical, so the real validator accepts it. Legal and clever, though the reused edge_id no longer names its true source, which an operator would likely want to rename. The model itself flagged this exact risk in its own warnings before being told to.

Declared a new edge_id (E_N10_MERGE) arriving at M08 instead of reusing E_N05_CONTINUE, which would change M08's expected_incoming -- correctly refused: 'expected_incoming must exactly equal the graph's declared incoming edges'. This is the V0.1 boundary working exactly as designed, not a defect. No numeric quality score: nothing usable was produced, but the refusal itself is the correct, intended outcome.

Schema-legal (passes validate_proposal/workflow_schema/routing_contract) but built on an incorrect runtime assumption: it declared conditional edges from N09 (an existing HUMAN_GATE) keyed on a verdict the runtime never produces or routes on, because workflow_runner.py unconditionally sets status=WAITING_FOR_HUMAN and returns the moment ANY HUMAN_GATE/FINAL_GATE completes (lines ~1529-1538) -- it never reaches routing_contract.evaluate_gate for that node type. The declared edges would never be evaluated at runtime. The planning package's `rules` said nothing about this. BEFORE the HUMAN_GATE clarification rule (see repair #1).

AFTER the HUMAN_GATE rule: same case, same profile, the model returned an EMPTY proposal (no nodes, no edges) rather than the confidently-wrong routable structure from before. Read positively: once correctly informed that a HUMAN_GATE's outgoing edges are runtime-dead, the model chose not to build a structure that looks functional but is not, rather than inventing a workaround the package gave it no basis for. This is the fail-closed direction, not a regression -- but it also means the operator's actual request (a gated follow-on step) still has no proposed answer; see 'remaining gaps' in the report.

For the deliberately under-specified 'make this more robust', the model built one bounded REVIEW->REPAIR->REVIEW loop and explicitly stated its interpretation as an assumption ('robustness means adding evidence-based independent review and at most one bounded repair cycle') rather than inventing open-ended structure. Legal and reasonably scoped; an operator would likely accept as-is or trim slightly.

Refused with 'node count exceeds limits.max_nodes'. This is IMPLEMENT_REVIEW_REPAIR_V1.json's OWN workflow-level limits.max_nodes=5 -- the fixture already has 5 nodes (N01-N05) at that cap, so ANY extension was structurally doomed regardless of proposal quality. The planning package DOES expose workflow.limits to the planner, but nothing in `rules` tells it the proposal's total node count must respect the workflow's own remaining budget, not just ProposalLimits.max_nodes=8. Partly a corpus-design artifact (this fixture happened to be full), partly a real, cheap, evidence-backed package gap -- see 'next recommendation'.

Fan-out into two REVIEW nodes (static analysis, dependency/supply-chain audit) converging on a MERGE ALL_REQUIRED, correctly role=None on the MERGE this time -- same failure class as B/C did NOT recur here, confirming the defect is a repeatable tendency, not a universal one.
